reviewer: claude-sonnet-5 (independent worktree review worker, no execution)

findings.summary: self.budget.check() runs before the try/except BudgetStopped block, so an already-expired deadline or pre-stopped budget raises an uncaught exception instead of the structured MORE_DILIGENCE result every other exhaustion path produces.
findings.fix: Move the initial check inside try, or wrap it separately and return the same structured dict with stop_reason='STOP_OR_DEADLINE'.
findings.test_to_add: run_case-style invocation with a past deadline or pre-stop()ped CallBudget asserting run() returns the structured dict, not a raised exception.

findings.summary: Merge key is (source_id, topic), omitting company_id. Safe only because one FactStore is created per run() call and the gateway already enforces company_id; not enforced at this layer.
findings.fix: Include company_id in the merge key.
findings.test_to_add: merge() facts for two companies sharing source_id/topic into one FactStore; assert both remain present under distinct keys.

findings.summary: When a ledger record for an existing source_id/topic gets a new content_sha256 ('identical source, changed content'), FactStore.merge silently overwrites the old Fact; no trace event distinguishes a new fact from a content replacement.
findings.fix: Have merge() report replaced vs. newly added keys; emit a SOURCE_CONTENT_REVISED trace event with old/new fact_id.
findings.test_to_add: Admit a fact for source-1/topic, then admit a second differently-hashed VerifiedRecord for the same source_id/topic; assert a revision trace event exists and the old fact_id is gone from admitted_fact_ids but present in trace history.

findings.location: guards.py:85 (TemporalGateway ledger keyed by source_id only)
findings.summary: Ledger dict is keyed solely by source_id with no company namespace. Fails safe (held, never wrongly admitted) if two companies share a source_id in one ledger, but silently withholds legitimate evidence for one of them -- an availability bug that looks like normal HELD behavior in review.
findings.fix: Namespace ledger keys by (company_id, source_id), or assert source_id uniqueness per company at construction.
findings.test_to_add: Two companies' VerifiedRecords sharing one raw source_id string in one ledger dict; assert the correct company's candidate is admitted and the other is held.

findings.summary: No test drives two full ClosedLoopRuntime.run() calls for different companies against one shared mutable cache dict; existing cache test only compares cache_key() strings, not runtime behavior.
findings.test_to_add: Run SYNTHETIC_COMPANY and a second company fixture through one shared cache={} instance; assert each result's admitted_fact_ids only contains that company's facts.

findings.summary: The 'CDX lists a capture but replay fetch failed entirely' branch (served_capture is None) is never exercised by any test; only the 'returned a different capture' (SUBSTITUTED_CAPTURE) branch is tested.

The no-leak assertion for rejection metadata (no future text/URL in rejection) is tested only for the first-seen SOURCE_HELD path, not for CACHED_SOURCE_HELD, which uses the same dict shape when a cached fact is revalidated and rejected.
findings.test_to_add: Admit a future-dated fact into cache via a permissive ledger, re-run with a ledger that rejects it, assert CACHED_SOURCE_HELD trace entries leak no text/URL.

findings.summary: used[kind] increments only after the concurrency check, so CONCURRENCY_CAP rejections are free to retry while CALL_CAP-eligible dispatched attempts stay charged. Correct and intended but undocumented as an invariant and untested as a reject-then-retry sequence.
findings.test_to_add: Hold one reservation open at concurrency=1; second reservation raises CONCURRENCY_CAP with used unchanged; release first; retry succeeds and used increments exactly once.

findings.summary: A Committee returning INVEST/PASS together with non-empty essential_gaps is silently downgraded to MORE_DILIGENCE via the generic 'if result is None or gaps or stop!=...' branch, with no distinguishing trace event. FixtureCommittee never produces this combination, so the case is wholly untested.
findings.fix: Explicitly raise or emit a dedicated trace event when decision in (INVEST, PASS) and essential_gaps is non-empty.
findings.test_to_add: Committee double returning INVEST with non-empty essential_gaps; assert the runtime treats this as an invariant violation, not a silent pass-through.

findings.summary: TOCTOU window between resolve(strict=True) and read_text(). Acceptable for a single-process offline fixture; live deployment needs OS-level sandboxing, not just path-allowlist checks.
findings.fix: Out of scope for offline module; needed only for live workers.

findings.summary: Shared cache dict is mutated without a lock. Fine today since run() dispatches research tasks sequentially despite RunRequest.concurrency being validated as a field; real parallel specialist dispatch is not implemented in ClosedLoopRuntime.run() yet.
findings.fix: Add locking before introducing real concurrent dispatch inside run().

findings.summary: Whole-document content_sha256 binding is a safe default for 'future fact embedded in structured profile field', but depends entirely on the live retrieval adapter hashing text that was actually confirmed pre-cutoff at the granularity it later claims. Not a fixable bug in the reviewed offline code.
findings.fix: Live-adapter design question for future work.

findings.summary: CallBudget assumes its injected clock always returns a timezone-aware datetime; a naive-datetime clock makes aware() raise ValueError instead of BudgetStopped, which ClosedLoopRuntime.run() does not catch.
findings.fix: Assert clock-returns-aware at CallBudget construction if ever wired to an external clock.

findings.summary: [a-z0-9.-]+\.[a-z]{2,} accepts malformed domains such as 'a..com' because the greedy group can absorb a double dot. Not security-relevant today since domain only feeds cache_key hashing and fixture URL construction, not a trust decision.
findings.fix: Tighten regex before domain drives any live retrieval policy.

findings.location: n/a (no live committee adapter exists yet)
findings.summary: Stale fact_revision/argument_revision rejection is proven only against a deliberately-stale fixture Committee double; whether a real LangGraph-backed adapter's own internal checkpointing could bypass the coordinator-side check cannot be assessed offline.

Residual pretrained future-knowledge leakage into CommitteeResult.rationale or essential_gaps text cannot be tested offline since no model runs in this prototype; remains an explicit limitation per R001_agent_reuse_decision.md.

explicitly_not_proposed: Hiding raw source text from the committee after an LLM has already seen it -- design already keeps rejected/unadmitted text inside the gateway (guards.py:107, runtime.py:90,99); only edge-case tests around that boundary are proposed.

Claiming schema omission (e.g. a CompanySeed lacking funding_total) by itself prevents file access -- file access is correctly gated by WorkspaceReader's explicit allowlist/root-containment check (guards.py:124-130), a separate necessary control.

fixture_table_cross_check.notes: Numbering follows the 16-row adversarial fixture table in R001_offline_prototype_acceptance.md in order of appearance.

root_note: Worker review only; root log records tested fixes and outstanding limitations.
